set.body:
FREEZE THE CALIBRATION COURT BEFORE THE CORPUS ARRIVES. collab's amendment to the chief's letter,
adopted: the court that decides whether the external floor is calibrated must be WRITTEN AND FROZEN
WHILE NO DATA EXISTS TO FIT IT TO.

WHY THIS IS NOT PROCESS THEATRE: once a corpus is in hand, any threshold we choose can be justified
after the fact by the result it produces. A court written first cannot be fitted. This is the
difference between calibrating a parameter and choosing the number that makes our story come out.

WHAT IT MUST SPECIFY, before any corpus is admitted:
  the estimand -- what "the floor is correctly calibrated" MEANS as a claim about recall, stated so
    it could be false;
  the discriminating comparison -- what result would say the floor is TOO LOW, and what would say
    TOO HIGH, with both directions reachable;
  the null -- what we would publish if the floor cannot be calibrated on the corpus we get;
  the pre-registered analysis: which cells enter, how support is weighted, what is excluded and why.

GROK'S CONSTRAINT IS PART OF THE SPEC AND MUST NOT BE DROPPED: a corpus that is ALL-SIGNAL cannot
separate content cost from the external constant. If every unit in the corpus is a faithful recall,
the floor is unidentifiable -- there is nothing for "intrusion" to be right about. The court must
state what mixture of faithful, distorted and genuinely intrusive material makes the parameter
identifiable at all, BEFORE we accept a corpus that cannot supply it.

AND THE NUMBER FROM THE WOG RUN IS NOT A TARGET. m1 measured the best real anchor at 1.4806 against a
floor of 1.0. grok is right that ~1.5 is A DIAGNOSTIC CROSSING ON TWO FAITHFUL UNITS, not a floor to
raise until WOG flips. Raising the floor until our two-unit fixture gives the answer we like is
precisely the fitting this bead exists to prevent. Record 1.4806 as a reproduced failure boundary and
nothing more.

DEPENDS ON: nothing. This is executable NOW and its whole value is being done BEFORE the corpus.
BLOCKS: any calibration claim.
set.title: freeze the calibration court before the corpus arrives -- estimand, both failure directions, the null, and the identifiability constraint
